title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What does California's "or its absence" clause mean for an organization that has never tested `[V]`?
options: It is protected, since there are no findings to disclose
It has not avoided the question — the absence of testing is itself relevant to a discrimination claim
It must begin testing within a defined period
It is presumed compliant until a complaint is filed
questions.explanation: Not testing is an answer rather than an avoidance. Set alongside Connecticut's mitigation framework, the direction is unmistakable: the existence and quality of your programme is legally consequential.

questions.prompt: Why must you run both the four-fifths rule and a standard deviation test?
options: Because different jurisdictions require different tests
Because four-fifths applies to hiring and standard deviation to promotion
Because four-fifths tells you whether a gap is large and standard deviation tells you whether it is real — only the first chases noise, only the second dismisses real harm in small populations
Because vendors compute one and regulators the other
questions.explanation: The two failure modes point in opposite directions, which is why a vendor report containing only one is incomplete regardless of which one it contains.

questions.prompt: 200 men apply and 60 are selected; 100 women apply and 21 are selected. What is the four-fifths ratio, and what should you do next?
options: 0.35 — investigate immediately
0.70 — flagged, and the next step is a standard deviation test to establish whether the result is statistically meaningful
0.21 — the disparity is severe
1.43 — men are disadvantaged
questions.explanation: 21/100 = 21%, 60/200 = 30%, ratio 0.70, below the 0.8 threshold. With 300 applicants the standard deviation test is likely to be meaningful; at 25 applicants it typically wouldn't be, even with an alarming ratio.

questions.prompt: Which step of proxy detection produces evidence about a less-discriminatory alternative?
options: Listing the model's inputs including derived features
Testing each input's association with protected characteristics in your own population
Testing the model with the variable removed, and comparing what happens to accuracy and to the disparity
Asking whether the variable is job-related
questions.explanation: That comparison is the most useful artifact the method produces, because less-discriminatory alternatives are precisely the ground on which disparate impact cases are contested.

questions.prompt: Why does external benchmarking conceal the problem it appears to measure?
options: Because benchmark data is usually out of date
Because when a problem concentrates in a minority of firms, a firm in the bad tail benchmarks as normal — the tail is inside the average it's compared against
Because industries define protected groups inconsistently
Because benchmarks exclude small employers
questions.explanation: Plus three compounding issues: comparators self-select, denominator definitions drift, and — decisively — the legal standard was never comparative. Being average is not a defence and never has been.

questions.prompt: What changed when AI removed the friction from adverse impact analysis?
options: The analysis became more accurate
The question moved from whether to run it to who may run it, under what protection, and what happens to the output — because in an organization where forty people can, somebody will
Testing became legally required in more jurisdictions
The results became admissible in a way they previously weren't
questions.explanation: Friction was never a good control — it suppressed useful analysis alongside risky analysis — but it was a control, and its removal means the realistic choice is between deliberate protected generation and casual unprotected generation.

questions.prompt: On what reasoning did a court hold bias-testing data privileged `[V]`?
options: Because it was marked confidential and stored with legal records
Because trade secret protection covered the underlying methodology
Because counsel curated the data and used the results in providing legal advice
Because the data was produced after litigation commenced
questions.explanation: That is a structure you build deliberately in advance. An analysis run on a Tuesday and forwarded to legal on Friday was not commissioned by counsel to inform advice, and labelling it later does not make it privileged.

It does not survive more than one litigation
It does not make the problem go away, does not survive waiver, does not cover underlying facts, and does not immunize the practice — only the analysis
It does not apply where a regulator rather than a plaintiff requests the material
questions.explanation: An organization using privilege to keep knowing about a disparity while doing nothing has built exactly the record Connecticut's sixth criterion punishes — with the additional feature that it did so on legal advice.
